title: This Time with Feeling

canonicalEdition.name: First edition
canonicalEdition.sourceProvenance: Frozen web bundle only: bibliographic records, table-of-contents evidence, official publication metadata, and narrow secondary summary support. Paraphrase-first; no full text frozen.

anchorSummary: This chapter extends the survival story by focusing on repetition: the hard thing is not only enduring one crisis but staying mentally usable when the company demands another round of painful action.
coreClaim: A leader does not get to spend prior suffering as a coupon against future hard decisions; the job keeps demanding clear action even when the emotional reserves are thin.
distinctMechanism: Horowitz uses repeated operational and financing shocks to show that leadership toughness is not one breakthrough moment but the ability to keep deciding under recurring strain.
requiredAnchors: Turnaround pressure continues after the first survival phase rather than ending cleanly.
Strategic shifts carry emotional cost because the leader knows exactly how painful the next round may be.
The chapter deepens the book's realism by showing that repetition itself is one of the hard things.
specificApplications: Audit how cumulative stress changes a leader's decision quality.
Use repeated shocks to teach endurance without glamorizing exhaustion.
Show why leaders need methods, not just adrenaline, for recurring crisis.
commonMisreadings: Reading the chapter as merely another crisis recap instead of a lesson about cumulative leadership burden.
Assuming experience makes later hard calls emotionally easy.
hardEdgeRequirement: Hard mode must show how repeated pressure can distort judgment if the leader mistakes numbness for resilience.
thresholdQuestion: How do you keep making clean decisions when the cost of the last round is still in your system?
